AUDIENCE & TESTABILITY:
API audience: USER-FACING.
Harness testability: TESTABLE.
Scoring recommendation: include in main user-facing denominator.

ROOT CAUSE:
The documentation incorrectly claims that passing an unsupported format to `Thumbnails.Builder.outputFormat(String)` throws an `UnsupportedFormatException`. In reality, `outputFormat()` eagerly validates the format and throws an `IllegalArgumentException` immediately. Because `UnsupportedFormatException` has a public constructor, the simplest and most deterministic way to test its `getFormatName()` method is to instantiate the exception directly.

CORRECT USAGE:
```java
String expectedFormat = "superfakeformat";
net.coobird.thumbnailator.tasks.UnsupportedFormatException ex = 
    new net.coobird.thumbnailator.tasks.UnsupportedFormatException(expectedFormat, "Format not supported");

String actualFormat = ex.getFormatName();

assert expectedFormat.equals(actualFormat) : "Format name should match the unsupported format requested";
System.out.println("__CHECK__ getFormatName " + actualFormat);
```

REQUIRED TYPES & IMPORTS:
net.coobird.thumbnailator.tasks.UnsupportedFormatException

DOC MUST SAY:
- `Thumbnails.Builder.outputFormat(String)` eagerly validates the format and throws an `IllegalArgumentException` if it is unsupported, NOT an `UnsupportedFormatException`.
- `UnsupportedFormatException` is typically thrown deeper in the pipeline during read/write task execution when the underlying Image I/O fails to process a format.
- For testing or programmatic creation, `UnsupportedFormatException` can be directly instantiated using its public constructor: `new UnsupportedFormatException(String formatName, String message)`.
